text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.74% today as oil prices held firm and refining fundamentals showed strength. The company operates both upstream oil production and downstream refining assets, and today's move reflects two supporting tailwinds: Brent crude traded around $100 a barrel amid ongoing Middle East supply risks from Iranian tanker attacks and Houthi activity in the Red Sea, while Goldman Sachs warned that tight refinery capacity will keep diesel prices elevated through 2027, which improves margins for refiners converting crude into fuel.

The stock's broader 3.26% gain over two weeks fits into a wider refining industry boost — high diesel prices are creating a structural margin advantage for companies that can convert crude into refined products, and geopolitical friction in major shipping chokepoints has lifted oil prices enough to support both exploration-and-production divisions and refining operations simultaneously.
